mainTopic: Why a widow may sell for her כתובה without בית דין, and when she loses that right after selling part of her כתובה
overview: Earlier, the משנה taught that a widow may sell her late husband's property for her כתובה without going to בית דין. The גמרא asks why this applies even to a widow from אירוסין. עולא says it is because of חינא: חכמים wanted women to be appealing to marry. רבי יוחנן says a husband does not want his wife shamed in בית דין. These two reasons differ about a גרושה. The גמרא defends עולא twice: the line 'a גרושה sells only in בית דין' follows רבי שמעון, and the heirs who may sell privately are a daughter or sister, who also need חן. A new משנה then teaches that once a widow has sold or pledged part of her כתובה, she sells the rest only in בית דין, while the חכמים let her keep selling privately for her מזונות. The גמרא says this first opinion is רבי שמעון, who holds that selling even half her כתובה costs her the מזונות. It asks whether the dispute is about 'part of the money is like all of it.' It then shows that the related dispute about a בוגרת marrying a כהן גדול comes only from how each side reads the פסוק.

steps.title: Why may a widow from betrothal sell without court?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason a widow from אירוסין may sell property without בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a widow from betrothal, what is the reason she may sell without court?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה lets a widow from אירוסין sell property on her own, without בית דין. This question sets up two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow from נישואין was already explained just before this. The word אלא ('but') shows that this case is harder to explain. Some new reason is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage, before the couple lives together
What is the reason?
But (here it signals a harder case)

phrases.english: But from betrothal, what is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means a woman whose husband died after betrothal, before the wedding. The משנה lets her sell without בית דין too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the earlier explanation of the widow from נישואין and moves on to the harder case of אירוסין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a widow from אירוסין may sell for her כתובה without בית דין.

steps.title: עולא: so that women are appealing to marry
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the reason is חינא, making women desirable for marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Because of desirability.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives his reason. Letting her sell without בית דין is one of the ways חכמים made women more appealing to marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For עולא, the rule is about how women look to future husbands. It does not depend on her relationship with her late husband. A rule like this could apply to any woman who is collecting a כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the name of a Talmudic sage
Grace or desirability, so that men will want to marry women

phrases.english: Ulla said: Because of desirability.
phrases.notes: The idea is that חכמים made this easier for women so that men would be glad to marry them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule exists because of חינא, to make women desirable to marry.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a husband doesn't want his wife shamed in court
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that a man does not want his wife shamed by appearing in בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Because a man does not want his wife to be shamed in court.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different reason. A husband would not want his wife shamed by having to go through בית דין, so the rule follows what he would want.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the reason comes from the husband's feelings about his wife. That means the reason holds only where he still cares about her. The next steps depend on this point.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל
That she be shamed or disgraced
Rabbinical court

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Because a man does not want
his wife to be shamed in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אָדָם רוֹצֶה שֶׁתִּתְבַּזֶּה אִשְׁתּוֹ בְּבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 1 that competes with עולא's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule exists because a husband does not want his wife shamed in בית דין.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the reasons of עולא and רבי יוחנן lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a case where these two reasons would give different rulings. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons explain the widow from אירוסין equally well. So the גמרא looks for a practical case where they split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is between them?
phrases.notes: He means: in what real case would these two reasons lead to a different ruling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers given in steps 2 and 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where the reasons of עולא and רבי יוחנן give different rulings.

steps.title: The difference is a divorcée
steps.stepSummary: The reasons differ about a גרושה. For עולא she may sell without בית דין, and for רבי יוחנן she may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a divorcée. According to the one who says 'because of desirability,' a divorcée also needs desirability. According to the one who says 'because a man does not want his wife shamed in court,' he does not care about a divorcée.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the two reasons split over a divorced woman. עולא's reason covers her, but רבי יוחנן's reason does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A divorced woman still needs to be appealing to marry, so עולא's reason applies to her as well. Her ex-husband no longer cares if she is shamed, so רבי יוחנן's reason does not apply. Under רבי יוחנן, then, a גרושה would have to sell through בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: A divorced woman
According to the one who says
He does not care
Needs desirability

steps.whatToRemember: For עולא, a גרושה may sell without בית דין because she too needs חן. For רבי יוחנן, she must use בית דין because her ex-husband no longer cares about her being shamed.

phrases.english: Between them is a divorcée.
According to the one who says, because of desirability:
a divorcée also needs desirability;

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אָדָם רוֹצֶה
phrases.english: according to the one who says, because a man does not want
his wife to be shamed in court:
about a divorcée he does not care.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גרושה: under עולא she sells without בית דין, and under רבי יוחנן she needs בית דין.

steps.title: Challenge to עולא from the משנה about a divorcée
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a גרושה sells only in בית דין. That fits רבי יוחנן but seems to contradict עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: And a divorcée may sell only in court. Granted, according to the one who says a man does not want his wife shamed in court, he does not care about a divorcée. But according to the one who says 'because of desirability,' a divorcée also needs desirability!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה, which says a divorcée may sell only in בית דין. It uses this line to attack עולא's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 showed that רבי יוחנן's reason requires a גרושה to use בית דין, so the משנה fits him well. Under עולא, though, a גרושה also needs חן and should be allowed to sell without בית דין. The משנה seems to say the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
Granted, it works well for...
She may not sell

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: וּגְרוּשָׁה לֹא תִּמְכּוֹר אֶלָּא בְּבֵית דִּין.
phrases.english: We learned: And a divorcée may sell only in court.
phrases.notes: This line actually comes from the next משנה, which you'll see below in step 14.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
because a man does not want
his wife to be shamed in court:
about a divorcée he does not care.
But according to the one who says, because of desirability,
a divorcée also needs desirability!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: וּגְרוּשָׁה לֹא תִּמְכּוֹר אֶלָּא בְּבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the difference found in step 5 to a line in the משנה and challenges עולא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under עולא, a גרושה needs חן just like a widow, so she should be allowed to sell without בית דין. The משנה requires בית דין for her.

steps.title: That line follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's line about a גרושה follows רבי שמעון, so it does not disprove עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא. It says the line about a divorcée belongs to רבי שמעון, not to the first opinion in the משנה that עולא is explaining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון holds that any woman who does not get food support sells only in בית דין. A divorcée gets no food support, so this line follows his rule. עולא is explaining the first opinion in the משנה, so this line does not contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
A תנא who disagrees in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not reject the line about a divorcée. It only says the line follows רבי שמעון, so it cannot be used against עולא, who is explaining a different opinion in the same משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: The line 'a גרושה sells only in בית דין' follows רבי שמעון, so עולא's reason of חינא still stands.

phrases.english: Whose is this? It is Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the line to a different opinion (it follows רבי שמעון)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line about a גרושה seemed to be the view of the first opinion in the משנה, which would disprove עולא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line follows רבי שמעון, who requires בית דין for any woman without food support. עולא explains the first opinion, so the line does not contradict him.

steps.title: If it follows רבי שמעון, the line about a גרושה seems unnecessary
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון already taught that a widow from אירוסין sells only in בית דין, so why teach the same thing again about a גרושה?
steps.simpleTranslation: If this line follows רבי שמעון, he already taught in the earlier clause: 'From betrothal she may not sell (except in court).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 7. If the line about a גרושה follows רבי שמעון, it seems to repeat something he already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's reason is that a woman without מזונות must sell in בית דין. A widow from אירוסין gets no מזונות, and neither does a גרושה. So the rule for the גרושה looks like it was already covered.

keyTerms.meaning: The first or earlier clause of the משנה
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage before the couple lives together
If

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Shimon,
but he already taught it in the first clause:
"From betrothal she may not sell, etc."?
phrases.notes: The "etc." stands for the rest of his words: she sells only in בית דין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 7 by claiming the line it explains would be repetitive
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה's line about a גרושה follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's earlier ruling about a widow from אירוסין already covers every woman without מזונות, so the line about a גרושה adds nothing new.

steps.title: A גרושה might seem to need her חן more
steps.stepSummary: The line is needed because we might have thought a גרושה, who needs her חן more, may sell outside בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: a widow from betrothal does not have a great need for her desirability, but a divorcée, who has a great need for her desirability, should be allowed to protect it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה must teach the case of the גרושה separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow from אירוסין does not depend much on her חן, so going to בית דין costs her little. A גרושה depends on it much more, so we might have let her sell privately. The משנה teaches that she still sells only in בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest you say. Introduces a mistaken idea the text comes to prevent
Charm or desirability, how well she is regarded
Great or abundant

phrases.english: Lest you say:
a widow from betrothal
is the one whose need for her desirability is not great,
but a divorcée,
whose need for her desirability is great,
say that she needs desirability.
phrases.notes: He means she should be allowed to sell without going to court, so her standing is not hurt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by showing the line about a גרושה is not repetitive
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: the line prevents a mistaken conclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גרושה, who needs her חן more, may sell without בית דין
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a גרושה sells only in בית דין, so the משנה had to say it

steps.title: The general rule about anyone without מזונות seems to cover the גרושה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's general rule, 'anyone who has no מזונות', seems to be there to include a גרושה. That would make the separate line repetitive again.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned this already: 'Anyone who has no sustenance (sells only in court).' What does that come to include? Is it not to include a divorcée?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge. Another phrase in the משנה seems to cover the גרושה already.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the reasoning about חן explains the line, a general rule usually exists to add cases not mentioned openly. The obvious added case is a גרושה, so her separate line looks extra again.

keyTerms.meaning: This too we already learned
Sustenance, the food and support a husband must provide
To include or bring in an extra case

phrases.english: This too we have learned:
"Anyone who does not have sustenance."
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון's general rule in the משנה: such a woman sells only in בית דין.

phrases.english: To include what?
Is it not to include a divorcée?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the charge of repetition by pointing to a different phrase in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משנה's separate line about a גרושה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general rule 'anyone without מזונות' must add some case, and the natural one is the גרושה, so her separate line is extra.

steps.title: The general rule includes a woman who is 'divorced and not divorced'
steps.stepSummary: The general rule does not come for a regular גרושה. It includes a woman whose divorce is doubtful, following רבי זירא, who says her husband must still give her מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it comes to include a woman who is 'divorced and not divorced,' following רבי זירא. רבי זירא said: wherever they said a woman is 'divorced and not divorced,' the husband must provide her sustenance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the general rule teaches about a different case: a woman whose divorce is in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule makes everything depend on whether she gets מזונות. רבי זירא says a woman with a doubtful divorce still gets מזונות from her husband. So the rule teaches us about her case, and the separate line about a regular גרושה is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Divorced and not divorced: a woman whose divorce is in doubt
An אמורא whose ruling is quoted here
Husband

steps.whatToRemember: The line about a גרושה is not extra. It blocks the idea that her need for חן lets her sell privately. The general rule about מזונות is about a different case, the doubtful divorcée, who per רבי זירא still gets מזונות.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two women. A regular גרושה gets no מזונות and sells only in בית דין. A 'divorced and not divorced' woman still gets מזונות from her husband, so the rule about women without מזונות does not put her in the same group.

phrases.english: No, it comes to include
"divorced and not divorced"
phrases.notes: A woman whose divorce is unclear, so she is treated as possibly still married.

phrases.english: in accordance with Rabbi Zeira.
For Rabbi Zeira said:
Wherever they said
"divorced and not divorced,"
the husband is obligated to provide her sustenance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 by giving the general rule a different purpose
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the general rule a different case to teach about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The general rule 'anyone without מזונות' exists to include a גרושה
steps.terutzMaskana: The general rule teaches about the doubtful divorcée, who gets מזונות per רבי זירא, so the line about a גרושה is still needed
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps Step 7's answer standing: the line about a גרושה can follow רבי שמעון without being repetitive, so the משנה does not disprove עולא.

steps.title: Her heirs may also sell outside court, so what חן do they need?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a widow's heirs may also sell outside בית דין. That fits the 'no shame' reason, but not עולא's reason of חן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Just as she sells outside court, so too her heirs, the ones who inherit her כתובה, sell outside court. This works for the view that a man does not want his wife shamed in court. Just as he does not want her shamed, he does not want her heirs shamed either. But for the view that the reason is her חן, what חן do her heirs have?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge עולא, who said a widow sells outside בית דין to protect her חן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets the widow's heirs sell outside בית דין too. If the reason is that the husband does not want his family shamed in court, that covers the heirs as well. But if the reason is protecting her חן so she can remarry, her heirs seem to have no such need.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. It brings a source to prove or challenge something.
Her heirs
She will be shamed or embarrassed
Charm or good name, which helps a woman find a new husband
This works well for one view... but for the other view there is a problem

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Just as she sells outside of court,
phrases.notes: 'She' is the widow, selling her late husband's property to collect her כתובה.

phrases.english: so too her heirs, those who inherit her כתובה,
sell outside of court.
This works well for the one who says
it is because a man does not want
his wife to be shamed in court.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאִיהִי לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ דְּתִתְבַּזֵּי —
phrases.english: Just as he is not happy that she should be shamed,

phrases.aramaic: יוֹרְשֶׁיהָ נָמֵי לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ דְּלִיבַּזּוּ,
phrases.english: he is also not happy that her heirs should be shamed.
But for the one who says it is because of her charm,
what charm is there for her heirs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending עולא from the משנה about a גרושה, the גמרא brings a new challenge to עולא from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's reason that a widow sells outside בית דין because of her חן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Heirs have no need for חן, yet the ברייתא lets them sell outside בית דין. Only the 'no shame' reason explains that.

steps.title: עולא: The heirs are her daughter or sister
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains the ברייתא as speaking about heirs who also need חן, such as her daughter or sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא explained it: For example, when her daughter or her sister inherited from her.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the challenge by narrowing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not talking about every kind of heir. It is talking about female heirs, like a daughter or sister, who also need their חן to find a husband. So the reason of חן still applies to them.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, meaning he applied the source to a specific case
For example, such as
Her sister

steps.whatToRemember: עולא keeps his reason of חן. Even the heirs who sell outside בית דין are women, like a daughter or sister, who also need their good name.

phrases.english: Ulla explained it:
for example, when her daughter or her sister inherited from her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the heirs are women who also need חן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Heirs in general have no need for חן, so the ברייתא seems to disprove עולא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks about a daughter or sister, who also need חן, so עולא's reason fits.

steps.title: משנה: A woman who already sold part of her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: If she sold, pledged, or gave away all or part of her כתובה, the first opinion says she sells the rest only in בית דין. The חכמים say she may sell many times outside בית דין, for her מזונות. A גרושה sells only in בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If she sold her כתובה or part of it, pledged her כתובה or part of it, or gave her כתובה or part of it to someone else, she may sell the rest only in court. The חכמים say: She may sell even four or five times. She sells for her מזונות outside court, and writes, 'I sold for מזונות.' A גרושה may sell only in court.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks whether a widow who already gave up part of her כתובה may still sell the rest outside בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says that once she has sold or given away part of her כתובה, the rest may be sold only in בית דין. The חכמים say she may keep selling in small amounts outside בית דין to pay for her food, writing that the sale was for מזונות. A גרושה gets no מזונות, so she always sells in בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, the משנה
Part of it
She pledged it as security for a loan
The rest, what is left
Food and support a widow receives from her husband's estate
A divorced woman

steps.confusionAlert: 'She may sell even four or five times' is the opinion of the חכמים, and it argues with the first line. It is not an addition to the first opinion.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If she sold her כתובה or part of it,
or pledged her כתובה or part of it,
or gave her כתובה or part of it to someone else,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תִּמְכּוֹר אֶת הַשְּׁאָר אֶלָּא בְּבֵית דִּין.
phrases.english: she may sell the rest only in court.
And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹכֶרֶת הִיא אֲפִילּוּ אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה פְּעָמִים.
phrases.english: she may sell even four or five times.
And she sells for food and support outside of court,
and writes: 'I sold for food and support.'

phrases.aramaic: וּגְרוּשָׁה לֹא תִּמְכּוֹר אֶלָּא בְּבֵית דִּין.
phrases.english: And a divorced woman may sell only in court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion about why a widow sells outside בית דין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First opinion: after selling, pledging, or giving away part of her כתובה, she sells the rest only in בית דין. חכמים: she may sell many times outside בית דין for מזונות. A גרושה always sells in בית דין.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the first opinion of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Whose opinion is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by asking which תנא the first opinion follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion makes her sell the rest in בית דין after selling only part of her כתובה. The גמרא wants to find the source of this strict view.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא, the start of the גמרא's discussion
Who is it? Whose opinion?

phrases.english: GEMARA: Whose opinion is our משנה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds the first opinion of the משנה

steps.title: It is רבי שמעון: selling even half loses her מזונות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי שמעון. A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר takes away her מזונות only if she sold her whole כתובה, but רבי שמעון takes them away even for half.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי שמעון, as a ברייתא teaches: If she sold her כתובה, pledged her כתובה, or made her כתובה an אפותיקי for someone else, she has no מזונות. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי שמעון says: Even if she sold or pledged only half of her כתובה, she lost her מזונות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first opinion of the משנה is רבי שמעון, and brings a ברייתא to show his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, selling even part of her כתובה makes her lose her מזונות. A widow sells outside בית דין only to pay for her food, so once she has no מזונות she must sell the rest in בית דין. רבי מאיר takes away her מזונות only when she sells the whole כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
A field set aside as the specific payment source for a debt
Half of it
She lost

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Shimon.
As it is taught: If she sold her כתובה,
or pledged her כתובה,
or made her כתובה a set payment source for someone else,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהּ מְזוֹנוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: she has no food and support. These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מָכְרָה וְלֹא מִשְׁכְּנָה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ
phrases.english: even though she did not sell or pledge her כתובה
except for half of it, she lost her food and support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first opinion is רבי שמעון, who holds that selling even half her כתובה makes her lose her מזונות, so she must sell the rest in בית דין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the right to sell outside בית דין to having מזונות. Once she loses her מזונות, she loses that right too.

steps.title: Do they argue about whether part of the money counts as all of it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי שמעון holds that part of the money is not like all the money, while the רבנן hold that it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that רבי שמעון holds we do not say part of the money is like all the money, and the רבנן hold we do say part of the money is like all the money?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to explain the argument between רבי שמעון and the רבנן as a bigger general principle. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, the half that is left is not treated as a full כתובה, so she is like a woman with no כתובה and loses her מזונות. For the רבנן, the part that is left counts like the whole כתובה, so she keeps her מזונות. The גמרא asks whether this is really the root of their argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? It suggests an idea that the גמרא may question
Part of the money is treated like all of the money
We say, we apply this rule

phrases.english: Is this to say that Rabbi Shimon holds

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא אָמְרִינַן מִקְצָת כֶּסֶף כְּכׇל כֶּסֶף,
phrases.english: that we do not say part of the money is like all the money,
phrases.notes: He means the half of the כתובה she still has does not count as a full כתובה.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold
that we do say part of the money is like all the money?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא of step 16 and tries to find the general principle behind the argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the argument between רבי שמעון and the רבנן is about the principle 'part of the money is like all the money'

steps.title: A ברייתא about the כהן גדול seems to show the opposite views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that a ברייתא about a בוגרת marrying a כהן גדול seems to show רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון holding the reverse of what was just suggested.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we heard them say the opposite! A ברייתא teaches: "And he shall take a wife in her virginity" excludes a בוגרת, whose signs of virginity have worn away. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון allow a בוגרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion from the last step. It brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון seem to hold the reverse positions on whether part counts like the whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the כתובה case, רבי שמעון is the one who treats a partial sale like a full sale. In this ברייתא, רבי מאיר treats a בוגרת, whose virginity is only partly gone, as if it were fully gone, so she cannot marry a כהן גדול. רבי שמעון lets her marry, so for him partly gone does not count as fully gone. Each רבי seems to flip positions.

keyTerms.meaning: The opposite; the reverse
A girl who has fully grown up, past נערות
Her signs of virginity have worn away
They declare fit or permitted

steps.confusionAlert: A בוגרת did not lose her virginity through relations. Her signs simply wore away as she grew up (שכלו בתוליה). The question is whether this partial loss disqualifies her for a כהן גדול.

phrases.english: But we heard them say the opposite!
As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"And he shall take a wife in her virginity"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:13. This פסוק is about the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: this excludes a grown woman whose signs of virginity have worn away,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁירִין בְּבוֹגֶרֶת.
phrases.english: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון permit a grown woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggested explanation of the מחלוקת from step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון argue about whether part counts like the whole
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the בוגרת case, רבי מאיר treats a partial loss like a full loss and רבי שמעון does not. That is the reverse of their positions in the כתובה case.

steps.title: They argue about the פסוק, and here is how רבי מאיר reads it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in the כהן גדול case they argue about how to read the words of the פסוק. It then explains רבי מאיר's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: There they argue about the פסוקים. רבי מאיר holds: the word "virgin" alone would mean even partial virginity is enough. "Her virginity" means she needs her full virginity. "In her virginity" teaches that relations in the normal way take away her virginity, but relations in an unusual way do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. In the כהן גדול case, the dispute comes from how each רבי reads the פסוק, not from a general rule about part and whole. It starts with רבי מאיר's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the plain word בתולה would have allowed partial virginity. The longer form בתוליה adds a requirement of complete virginity, so a בוגרת is excluded. The extra letter ב in בבתוליה teaches a separate law, that only normal relations end her status as a virgin.

keyTerms.meaning: פסוקים, verses
Part of
In the normal way of relations
In an unusual way of relations

steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the contradiction. Each רבי's ruling on the כהן גדול comes from the wording of the פסוק, so it tells us nothing about his general view on part and whole.

phrases.english: There they argue about the verses.
רבי מאיר holds:
Had it said "virgin," that would mean even partial virginity is enough.
"Her virginity" means she needs her complete virginity.
"In her virginity": relations in the normal way, yes, they take away her virginity,
phrases.notes: This lesson comes from the extra letter ב at the start of the word.

phrases.english: relations in an unusual way, no, they do not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different basis: the dispute comes from reading the פסוק, not from a general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בוגרת dispute shows each רבי's general view on whether part counts like the whole
steps.terutzMaskana: The בוגרת dispute comes only from how each רבי reads the words of the פסוק, so it does not contradict their positions on the כתובה

steps.title: How רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון read the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון read the פסוק the other way: "virgin" alone means a complete virgin, and "her virginity" widens it to include partial virginity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון hold: the word "virgin" means a complete virgin. "Her virginity" means even partial virginity is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by giving the reading of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון. This is why they allow a בוגרת to marry a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their reading is the mirror image of רבי מאיר's. For them, the plain word בתולה would require a complete virgin, and the form בתוליה widens it to include a girl with only part of her virginity. So the בוגרת is permitted because of the wording, not because of a general view about part and whole.

keyTerms.meaning: Complete; whole
Implies; means
They hold

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge is answered. In the כהן גדול case, both sides argue only about how to read the פסוק, so no contradiction remains with their views on a widow who sold part of her כתובה.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון hold:
"Virgin" implies a complete virgin,
"her virginity" means even partial virginity is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 19 by giving the other side's reading
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different basis: the dispute comes from reading the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון permits a בוגרת because, in general, part does not count like the whole
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון permits a בוגרת only because of how he reads the words בתולה and בתוליה
